data.mechanism: SLC38A9 sits in the lysosomal membrane and reads arginine on the inside. Arginine-bound SLC38A9 acts as an exchange factor that loads RagA with GTP, switching the Rag dimer on (SHE2018B); it also pumps essential amino acids, including leucine, back out into the cytosol.
data.mechanism_beginner: SLC38A9 sits in the lysosome's wall, senses arginine inside, and then flips RagA into its "on" shape, telling the Rag proteins there's enough.
data.boundary: Mammalian cell studies and purified-protein work (REB2015, WAN2015, JUN2015, WYA2017, SHE2018B). Cell and biochemical evidence; whole-animal and human relevance are not tested here.
data.note: Five independent studies - one of the best-supported edges in the sensor branch.
